title: Optimizing Datalog for the GPU
problem: Modern Datalog engines designed for CPUs cannot efficiently exploit GPU parallelism due to the relational algebra operations over sparse, recursively updated fact sets that do not map well to dense GPU data structures. Existing GPU join implementations also carry high memory overhead for recursive workloads like points-to analysis.
motivation: High-throughput applications in static analysis, network monitoring, and social-media mining rely on Datalog engines, and GPU compute density offers large potential speedups that existing engines fail to capture.
method: GPUlog implements a Datalog engine backend on data center GPUs by introducing the Hash-Indexed Sorted Array (HISA), a novel range-indexed data structure that combines incremental range indexing (for efficient semi-naive evaluation of recursive Datalog) with dense array operations amenable to GPU throughput. Iterated relational algebra kernels (join, union, difference) are implemented over HISA, enabling GPU-native semi-naive evaluation with favorable memory footprint compared to GPU hash-join baselines.
key_novelty: The Hash-Indexed Sorted Array (HISA) data structure combines incremental range-indexed relation semantics with dense-array GPU throughput, enabling efficient recursive Datalog evaluation on GPUs.
contributions: Design and implementation of GPUlog, a GPU backend for in-memory Datalog evaluation
The HISA data structure enabling range-indexed incremental relational algebra on GPUs
Up to 45x speedup over Souffle (CPU Datalog engine) on context-sensitive points-to analysis of httpd
Favorable memory footprint compared to contemporary GPU-based join implementations

metrics.speedup: up to 45x over Souffle on httpd points-to analysis

limitations: Evaluation focuses on points-to analysis; generality across all Datalog workload classes is not fully demonstrated.
